lesson.title: Benchmarks You Just Know

steps.say: You already know how to convert fractions into decimals and percents by dividing, like three eighths becoming zero point three seven five, or thirty seven point five percent. That works every time, but it is slow. Today we are building a tiny set of numbers you just know instantly, so you never have to stop and divide for the common ones.

Here is the trick that makes these stick: think of one whole as one dollar, one hundred cents, or one hundred percent. Cut that dollar into four equal parts and each part is twenty five cents. So one quarter is zero point two five, or twenty five percent. Two quarters is fifty cents, and three quarters is seventy five cents, which is zero point seven five, or seventy five percent. You are not memorizing, you are just counting quarters of a dollar.

visual.caption: From one quarter to three quarters on the zero to one line

steps.say: Now the sneaky one. One third means cutting the dollar into three equal parts, and one hundred does not split evenly into three. Three times thirty three is ninety nine, with one cent left over. So one third is about zero point three three, or about thirty three percent, and the threes go on forever. Notice where it sits on the line: just past a quarter, and nowhere near a half.

visual.caption: One third sits a little past one quarter

steps.say: Here is the mistake almost everyone makes: they see the three in one third and write zero point three, or thirty percent. Watch why that is wrong. Zero point three is three tenths. Three tenths plus three tenths plus three tenths is only nine tenths, which is ninety percent, not a whole dollar. But zero point three three three and so on, three times, really does fill the whole thing. So one third is a bit bigger than zero point three. On the line, thirty percent and thirty three percent are two different spots.

visual.caption: Zero point three is short of one third

steps.say: Let us use them. Say a hoodie at Metrotown is forty dollars and it is one quarter off. You do not divide anything. One quarter is twenty five percent, so a quarter of forty dollars is ten dollars off, and you pay thirty dollars. Now three quarters off would be seventy five percent, which is three lots of ten, so thirty dollars off and you pay ten. Same hoodie, and the benchmark did all the work in your head.

visual.caption: Twenty five cells is one quarter, seventy five cells is three quarters

steps.say: So lock these four in: one quarter is zero point two five and twenty five percent, one half is zero point five and fifty percent, three quarters is zero point seven five and seventy five percent, and one third is about zero point three three, never zero point three.

lesson.answer: One quarter is twenty five percent, three quarters is seventy five percent, and one third is about thirty three percent — not thirty.

practice.question: Your allowance is sixty dollars. Write each of these as a decimal and a percent, then find the dollar amount: one quarter of sixty dollars, and three quarters of sixty dollars. Then answer this in words: is one third of sixty dollars closer to eighteen dollars or to twenty dollars, and why?
practice.answer: One quarter is zero point two five, or twenty five percent, which is fifteen dollars. Three quarters is zero point seven five, or seventy five percent, which is forty five dollars. One third of sixty dollars is exactly twenty dollars, because one third is about zero point three three, not zero point three. Zero point three of sixty would only be eighteen dollars, so the answer is twenty dollars.
